summary: The note surveys innovations, policies and practices since September 2023 aimed at making internet infrastructure more resilient to outages. It covers self-healing networks, AI/ML tools, satellite redundancy, edge computing, quantum-resistant encryption, policy collaboration, redundancy regulation, community networks and workforce education. It concludes optimistically that a near-unbreakable internet is within reach.
one_line: Overview of technologies, regulations and community efforts since late 2023 that aim to reduce internet outages and build a resilient network.
key_facts: On November 10, 2023, a major internet provider suffered widespread outages from a fiber cut during construction, leaving thousands of businesses offline for hours.
Self-healing networks automatically detect and isolate failures and reroute data in real time to maintain service continuity.
Dr. Iris Bennett of TechForward said at a December 5, 2023 conference that the systems are 'not only reactive to issues as they arise but are also predictive'.
Since NetStable Inc. rolled out AI-enhanced tools in early January 2024, downtime has fallen by 35% compared to the previous year.
OrionCom and SkyWeave launched low Earth orbit satellite constellations with reduced latency and higher bandwidth.
On February 22, 2024, during a massive grid failure, satellite networks took over the load and kept critical communication lines open.
During a DDoS attack on April 8, 2024, edge computing nodes maintained uninterrupted service despite the larger network being targeted.
CyberLock has begun integrating quantum-resistant algorithms into its systems, which have so far proven immune to sophisticated intrusion attempts.
The International Summit on Cyber Resilience in Brussels on September 15, 2023 established the Global Resilience Partnership of tech companies, governments and NGOs.
The Network Redundancy and Preparedness Act (NRPA) followed the October 2023 Outage on the Eastern Seaboard and mandates redundancy, regular stress tests and public resilience reporting.
Lakeside Connect, a community network established in Minnesota on March 3, 2024, and run by local residents, weathered regional service outages.
Global Tech Education has launched initiatives to train the next generation of network engineers in innovation and cross-disciplinary skills.
